info.title: sol2flow API
info.description:
Programmatic access to sol2flow with a **personal API key** (Settings → API keys). A key acts as its owner with exactly the same permissions as in the app.

- **Authentication:** `Authorization: Bearer sf_…` on every request. Cookies are ignored.
- **Scopes:** a key has **full access** or is **read only**. Read-only keys may call GET (and HEAD) only — each operation names what it needs in `x-required-scope`; otherwise 403 `insufficient_scope`. Webhook endpoints need a full-access key.
- **Pagination:** list endpoints take `limit` (1–100, default 50) and `cursor`, and answer `{ "data": [...], "next_cursor": "…" | null }`.
- **Errors:** `{ "error": { "code", "message", "field"? } }` with 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 413, 422 or 429.
- **Rate limits:** 600 requests per 10 minutes per key, of which at most 120 writes (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE); 429 carries `Retry-After` (seconds).
- **Keys:** up to 25 active keys per account; they expire after 30, 90 or 365 days, or never.
- **Formats:** JSON, snake_case, timestamps ISO 8601 (UTC), dates `YYYY-MM-DD`.
- **Public:** operations tagged *Public* (e.g. `GET /public/plans`) need no key: read-only data for a website, CORS for any origin without credentials, cached for five minutes, rate-limited per IP.

post.summary: Move a task to another board
post.description: To a list of another board in the same workspace (422 `move_target` otherwise); needs edit rights on both boards. The task gets the target board’s next number (PRD-3 → OPS-17) and its old URL redirects. Comments, checklist, attachments, time and activity go along. Workspace labels stay; board labels are matched by name on the target board, created there if you may create board labels, else dropped. Assignees and members without access to the target board get it (members: Editor, guests: Viewer).

post.summary: Link the task to another task
post.description: Editors and board admins of this task (not archived); you must be able to open the other task, which must be in the same workspace (any board). `kind` is seen from this task: `blocked_by` stores “other blocks this”. One link per pair and type, whatever the direction: 409 `link_exists`; linking a task to itself: 422 `link_self`. Logs activity on both tasks, tells the blocked task’s people, emits `task_link.added`.

kind.description: The link as seen from the task in the path: `blocks` / `blocked_by`, `duplicates` / `duplicated_by`, `relates_to` (the same from both sides). The other task sees the inverse.

delete.description: From either task’s side: edit rights on the task in the path, view rights on the other one. A link you can’t see is 404. Emits `task_link.removed`.

post.description: Step 1 of 3. Editors and board admins. Answers the part size: send the file in `part_count` parts of `chunk_size` bytes (the last one smaller) with `PUT /uploads/{uploadId}/parts/{n}` (n from 1), then `POST /uploads/{uploadId}/complete`. With `task_id` the file is attached to that task. Limits: Admin → General → Uploads (413 file_too_large).

413.description: The file is larger than the instance allows (`max` in MB).

put.description: Step 2. Body: the part’s bytes (`Content-Type: application/octet-stream`), exactly its size. Re-sending a part replaces it.

post.description: Step 3: assembles the parts (409 upload_incomplete lists missing ones) and attaches the file to the task, if any.

patch.summary: Change access, default role or the public link
patch.description: Board admins (403 `forbidden` otherwise). `public_link: true` creates a read-only public link (or keeps the existing one), `false` removes it — a new link gets a new URL. An object sets the link’s expiry, password, a new URL (`regenerate`) and what visitors see. Anything but turning it off needs the organization’s plan to include public boards (403 `plan_feature`) and the workspace to allow public links (403 `public_links_disabled_workspace`). Changes are in the board’s activity and the audit log.

access.description: WORKSPACE: every workspace member gets `default_role`; RESTRICTED: only people added to the board

enabled.description: On: the read-only public link (a new link gets a new URL); off: removed (its settings are kept)

expires_at.description: When the link stops working (ISO 8601, in the future); null: never

password.description: Visitors must enter it (6–128 characters; stored as a hash, never returned); null removes it. A new or removed password signs out every visitor.

regenerate.description: A new URL; the old one stops working at once

visibility.description: What visitors see (omitted keys stay as they are). Defaults of a new link: labels, dates, checklists, descriptions on; assignees, members, comments, attachments, time off. Archived tasks never show; people only by name and photo.

post.summary: Add someone to a board (or change their role)
post.description: Board admins. `user_id` is someone in the workspace, or an existing account outside it that you can see in the app’s people picker (shares a workspace with you) — they are then added to the workspace too, as `workspace_role` (GUEST, the default; MEMBER needs a workspace admin, else 403) — like the Share dialog. Anyone else is 404: invite them by email with `POST /workspaces/{slug}/invitations` and `board_id`. Adding to an archived board isn’t possible for outsiders (409 `board_archived`). The person is notified. Lowering the last board admin: 409 `last_board_admin`. Guests are view-only: for a guest (or someone added as one) `role` can only be VIEWER — anything else is 403 `guest_viewer_only`; without `role` guests get VIEWER, everyone else EDITOR.

role.description: Default: VIEWER for guests, EDITOR for everyone else

workspace_role.description: Only for people outside the workspace (default GUEST); ignored otherwise

patch.description: Board admins. Only for people added to the board (404 otherwise). Demoting the last board admin: 409 `last_board_admin`. Guests can only be VIEWER (403 `guest_viewer_only`; make them a workspace member first).

delete.description: Board admins. They keep their workspace membership (and, on a WORKSPACE board, the default role). Removing the last board admin: 409 `last_board_admin`.

get.description: Anyone who can open the board. Addresses are masked (`j•••@client.io`) unless you are an instance admin, a workspace admin or sent the invitation; `q` only matches what you see. Invite with `POST /workspaces/{slug}/invitations` and `board_id`.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Address (as shown to you) or inviter name contains

get.description: Members and admins of the workspace, like the Members page (guests: 404 — they don’t see the Members page). Members by role, then name; with `include=invitations` the pending invitations follow (newest first, addresses masked unless you may see them). Emails of members only for instance admins.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Name or username contains (invitations: the address as shown to you, or the inviter)

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: `invitations`: list pending invitations after the members

post.summary: Add existing accounts to a workspace
post.description: Workspace admins. Only people you can see in the app’s people picker (who share a workspace with you; instance admins: everyone) are added — unknown, hidden, inactive ids and existing members are skipped silently. They are notified. To add anyone else, invite them by email.

patch.description: Workspace admins. Not your own role (403; use another admin), not memberships managed by OIDC group sync (403). Demoting the last explicit admin of a private workspace: 409 `last_private_admin`. Changing an instance admin’s automatic membership makes it explicit. Guests are view-only and never take a seat: making someone a GUEST keeps their boards as VIEWER; making a guest a MEMBER (“Make member”) takes a seat — 409 `plan_limit` (kind `seats`) when the plan has none left.

delete.description: Workspace admins. Not yourself (403: use `POST /workspaces/{slug}/leave`), not memberships managed by OIDC group sync (403); the last explicit admin of a private workspace: 409 `last_private_admin`. Their board roles, pins and task assignments in the workspace go too; they are notified.

post.description: Any role. 409 `last_admin_leave` for the last admin (promote someone first), `last_private_admin` for the last explicit admin of a private workspace, `oidc_managed` for memberships from OIDC group sync, `instance_admin_leave` for instance admins in a non-private workspace. Your board roles, pins and task assignments there go too; the admins are notified.

Workspace admins; with `board_id`, admins of that board may invite **guests** (`role: GUEST`) to it — other roles need a workspace admin (403). Guests are view-only: a guest invitation’s `board_role` can only be VIEWER (403 `guest_viewer_only`). Guest invitations count against the plan’s optional guest limit (each address as a new guest): 409 `plan_limit` with kind `guests` when they don’t fit. Every address gets an email with a link valid for 14 days (re-inviting replaces the pending invitation); accounts whose verified email matches also get an in-app notification. The answer is **the same whether or not an address has an account** — nobody is added directly. Rate limits like the app: 100 addresses per hour per inviter (`invite`) and 200 per workspace (`invite-workspace`); each address counts.

board_id.description: Also give access to this board (must be in the workspace)

get.description: Members and admins of the workspace (guests: 404). The address is shown in full only to instance admins, workspace admins and whoever sent the invitation; everyone else gets it masked (`j•••@client.io`), and `q` only matches what you see. `board_id` is null for boards you can’t open. One item per invitation: someone invited to the workspace and to two boards has three (the Members page shows them as one person).

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Address (as shown to you) or inviter name contains

delete.description: Workspace admins (any invitation), whoever sent it (while still in the workspace), and admins of the invitation’s board. Others: 403; unknown or no longer pending: 404. The invitee’s notification turns into “No longer valid”. Rate limit `invite-revoke` (100 per hour).

get.description: Pending, unexpired invitations to your **verified** email address (an unverified address matches nothing — verify it by opening an invitation link or ask an admin), like the banner in the app.

post.description: Accepts this invitation only; your other invitations to the workspace stay pending. Not in the workspace yet: you join it (with the highest role of your pending invitations to it). You get this invitation’s board role (guests: Viewer). Returns the workspace. 404 when it isn’t yours, not pending (or expired) or your email isn’t verified.

post.summary: Import boards from kan.bn or Trello
post.description: Workspace admins, with a full-access key. Starts a background import (202); poll GET …/imports/{id}. Sources: `kanbn` (API key; `base_url` for a self-hosted Kan), `trello` (API key + token), `trello_file` (a board JSON export in `board`, up to 50 MB). Credentials are only kept, encrypted, while the run needs them. Re-running an import adds what is new and never duplicates. One import per workspace at a time (409 `import_running`).

The public, non-archived plans in the Owner’s order, with prices, limits, features and highlights. `?locale=de` (also `de-DE`) picks the highlights’ language; unknown or missing: English. 404 where plans are off. CORS: any origin, no credentials; `Cache-Control: public, max-age=300`. Rate limit: 120 requests per minute per IP.

404.description: Plans are off on this instance.

email_verified.description: Whether `email` is verified (the emailed link was opened, an invitation to it was accepted, the identity provider vouched for it, or staff set it). False without an email. A new address waiting for its link isn’t shown until it is verified.

staff_role.description: Your staff role on this instance (OWNER, ADMIN, SUPPORT, AUDITOR), or null if you aren’t staff. Replaces `is_instance_admin`.

time_zone.description: Your saved IANA time zone (Settings → Preferences), e.g. `Europe/Berlin`; null = automatic: the app follows your browser. API timestamps are always UTC.

counts.description: boards, lists, labels, tasks, checklistItems, comments, attachments created; existing = skipped because imported before; totalTasks / doneTasks for progress

errors.description: Problems that did not stop the run (e.g. attachment_failed, board_failed)

bearerAuth.description: A personal API key from Settings → API keys. Scopes: a **full access** key may call every operation (within its owner’s permissions); a **read only** key only operations whose `x-required-scope` is `read` (GET / HEAD) — anything else answers 403 `insufficient_scope`.

BadRequest.description: Malformed request: body is not JSON, or a path / query parameter is invalid (`field`).

Unauthorized.description: No valid API key: missing, malformed, unknown, expired or revoked, or the account is disabled.

Forbidden.description: Your role doesn’t allow this (`forbidden`), the key is read-only (`insufficient_scope`), API keys / webhooks are switched off on this instance (`api_disabled`, `webhooks_disabled`), the organization’s plan doesn’t include it (`plan_feature` with `feature`, e.g. `api`), or its workspaces are read-only (`plan_read_only`: past due or canceled).

NotFound.description: It doesn’t exist, or you can’t open it (the API never says which).

Conflict.description: The current state doesn’t allow it, e.g. `board_archived`, `label_scope`, `last_board_admin`, `last_admin_leave`, `last_private_admin`, `oidc_managed`, `instance_admin_leave`, `conflict`, or a limit of the organization’s plan is reached (`plan_limit` with `kind`, `limit`, `used`).

Invalid.description: Validation failed: `code` names the rule (e.g. `title_required`, `too_long` with `max`, `dates_order`) and `field` the input.

TooManyRequests.description: Rate limit reached (`rate_limited`), or the organization’s daily API cap (`plan_limit` with `kind: apiCalls`, until midnight UTC); wait `Retry-After` seconds.
